records.claim_text: The project definition is the framework object under which every other project object is created.
records.evidence_quote: The project definition is a framework for all the objects created within a project.

records.claim_text: A project definition must exist before any WBS can be created; it is the mandatory first object.
records.evidence_quote: Before you create a WBS, you have to create a project definition.

records.claim_text: Project definition holds project-wide data such as start/finish dates, organizational data and planning parameters.
records.evidence_quote: The project definition contains data that affects the entire project (for example, start and finish dates, organizational data, and planning parameters).

records.claim_text: Project definition values act as defaults that are pushed down to WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: It contains default values that can be passed on to the WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Controlling area is fixed at project definition level and is unique for the whole project.
records.evidence_quote: The controlling area that you specify when you create a project definition is unique for the entire project.

records.claim_text: Controlling area cannot be overridden on an individual WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: The project definition's controlling area is valid for the entire project and cannot be changed for a WBS element.

records.claim_text: Plant, company code and business area may differ per WBS element even inside one project.
records.evidence_quote: You can assign different plants, company codes, and business areas to WBS elements.

records.claim_text: On creation or insertion, a WBS element copies organizational values down from the project definition.
records.evidence_quote: When you create new WBS elements or incorporate them into a WBS, the values from the project definition are copied into the WBS elements.

records.claim_text: The WBS is a hierarchical model of the project that organizes project tasks into a hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: The work breakdown structure (WBS) is a model of the project that organizes project tasks into a hierarchy.

records.claim_text: The WBS is the functional basis for downstream planning: process, cost, scheduling, capacity planning and costing.
records.evidence_quote: the functional basis for further planning steps in a project, for example, for process planning, cost planning, scheduling, capacity planning or costing.

records.claim_text: A WBS element is the structure element of the WBS and describes a task or a further-divisible partial task.
records.evidence_quote: Structure element of the work breakdown structure (WBS). A WBS element describes either a certain task or a partial task that can be subdivided further.

records.claim_text: WBS elements may be subdivided across arbitrarily many levels until the required level of detail is reached.
records.evidence_quote: You can divide these WBS elements at various levels until you reach the level of detail you require.

records.claim_text: Because the WBS is hierarchical, values summarize upward and are displayed on higher-level WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: Since the WBS is structured hierarchically, the data can be summarized and displayed at the corresponding higher-level WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Project hierarchies exist to aggregate data, allocate budget and define responsibility.
records.evidence_quote: Hierarchies are often used for the following purposes: Evaluating aggregated data, Allocating budgets, Defining responsibilities

records.claim_text: The WBS aggregates dates, costs and commitments coming from network activities.
records.evidence_quote: The work breakdown structure can be used to aggregate dates, costs, and commitments from the network activities.

records.claim_text: Revenue planning/actuals and budgeting sit on WBS elements, not on network activities.
records.evidence_quote: WBS elements themselves would be used for planned and actual revenues, and they can also be used for budgeting.

records.claim_text: Creating a WBS requires entering a project profile for the project.
records.evidence_quote: When you create a work breakdown structure, you must also enter a project profile for the project.

records.claim_text: The project profile supplies default values and processing parameters such as settlement schema and factory calendar.
records.evidence_quote: The project profile contains default values and parameters for processing the project, for example, which settlement schema is valid

records.claim_text: The chosen project profile is stored on the project definition once the WBS is created.
records.evidence_quote: If you create a work breakdown structure, the project profile is saved in the project definition.

records.claim_text: A project carries exactly one project profile; the profile type drives accounting behaviour.
records.evidence_quote: There can only be one project profile per project.

records.claim_text: Coding masks exist to render and structure complex project numbers for display and entry.
records.evidence_quote: Coding masks serve as a display option for complex project numbers.

records.claim_text: Mask syntax uses X for alphanumeric positions and 0 for numeric positions, plus special characters as separators.
records.evidence_quote: The following characters are available for editing and structuring project numbers: X for alphanumeric characters, and 0 for numeric characters and special characters.

records.claim_text: The mask that applies is selected by the leading characters of the project number, which act as the coding key.
records.evidence_quote: The way it is set up depends on the first characters of the project number.

records.claim_text: A mask can be extended later but never shortened once projects exist on it — numbering is effectively immutable.
records.evidence_quote: you cannot take anything away if WBSs have already been created using this project coding mask.

records.claim_text: A coding key can be blocked so that no new projects may be created under it.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot create new projects with this coding key if you maintain a blocking checkbox.

records.claim_text: The coding mask defines how WBS element IDs are derived from the project ID.
records.evidence_quote: The project coding mask defines how WBS element IDs are determined from the project ID.

records.claim_text: A WBS element ID including project ID and separators is capped at 24 characters.
records.evidence_quote: The total length of a WBS ID, including project ID and all special characters, must not exceed 24 characters.

records.claim_text: With a coding mask, the system derives hierarchy level from the WBS number; the shortest number becomes level 1.
records.evidence_quote: The WBS element with the shortest number is created in level 1.

records.claim_text: The mask must contain enough separators to represent every intended hierarchy level.
records.evidence_quote: enough dashes to model all the levels in the project hierarchy.

records.claim_text: A configurable special character acts as input help that auto-prefixes the parent WBS number during entry.
records.evidence_quote: the system copies the number of the higher-level WBS elements into the field.

records.claim_text: Operative indicators define what role a WBS element plays during project execution.
records.evidence_quote: You use operative indicators to define the characteristics of a WBS element and to specify what tasks the WBS element will perform during project execution.

records.claim_text: Planning element flags a WBS element as one on which costs may be planned.
records.evidence_quote: WBS elements for which you want to plan costs are flagged as planning elements.

records.claim_text: Account assignment element flags a WBS element as a valid target for actual cost postings.
records.evidence_quote: WBS elements to which you want to post actual costs are flagged as account assignment elements.

records.claim_text: Billing element flags a WBS element as one where revenue may be planned or posted.
records.evidence_quote: WBS elements where you want to plan or post revenues are flagged as billing elements.

records.claim_text: A billing element is a structure element (project or WBS element) against which revenue can be planned and posted.
records.evidence_quote: Billing Element is a project structure element against which a revenue can be planned and posted.

records.claim_text: Billing elements cannot nest: none may sit inside another billing element's subtree.
records.evidence_quote: A billing element cannot have another billing element in its subtree, nor can it be part of the subtree of another billing element.

records.claim_text: Every WBS element beneath a billing element inherits the same functional area and profit center.
records.evidence_quote: All the WBS elements in the subtree of a billing element must have the same functional area and profit center as the billing element.

records.claim_text: A revenue-bearing project must contain at least one billing element.
records.evidence_quote: A project with revenue must contain at least one billing element.

records.claim_text: Settlement rules may not be entered on WBS elements inside a billing element subtree.
records.evidence_quote: you will not be able to enter any settlement rule on the WBS elements in the billing element subtree.

records.claim_text: A network can only be assigned to a WBS element that is flagged as an account assignment element.
records.evidence_quote: To be able to assign a network to a WBS element, you must first identify the WBS element as an account assignment element.

records.claim_text: A profile checkbox can force the account assignment flag on for every WBS element in the project.
records.evidence_quote: The All Acct Asst Elem checkbox sets the account assignment checkbox for all WBS elements.

records.claim_text: A profile setting can restrict a project to a single top-level (root) WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: Using the Only One Root checkbox, you define that there can only be one top WBS element.

records.claim_text: The statistical flag decides whether a WBS element can be debited with real costs or only statistically.
records.evidence_quote: The Statistical checkbox determines whether costs can be debited from a WBS element or whether statistical costs can only be posted for it.

records.claim_text: Setting the statistical flag on a project propagates it to every WBS element in that project hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: When you set the statistical flag for a project, this flag applies to the WBS elements present in the project hierarchy.

records.claim_text: Statistical WBS elements can neither be settled nor carry overhead.
records.evidence_quote: Statistical WBS elements cannot be settled or carry overheads.

records.claim_text: The statistical indicator is set from the model order or project profile, or directly on the master record.
records.evidence_quote: You define the order or WBS element as 'statistical' by setting an indicator in the model order or the project profile.

records.claim_text: Project type is a classification attribute usable as a selection criterion in reporting.
records.evidence_quote: The Project Type can be used as a selection criterion in the Information System.

records.claim_text: A Level of Detail setting controls how many hierarchy levels are expanded when a project is opened.
records.evidence_quote: The Level of Detail field specifies the number of hierarchy levels that the system displays when a project is opened in a particular processing transaction.

records.claim_text: Tabular overviews can label WBS elements by key, short ID or description, configurably.
records.evidence_quote: The Display Options field determines whether WBS elements are mainly displayed according to key, short ID, or description in tabular overviews.

records.claim_text: A network represents the sequence of activities in a project (or of a single activity within it).
records.evidence_quote: A network can represent the sequence of activities in a project or the sequence of a single activity within a project.

records.claim_text: Networks are the basis for planning, analyzing, controlling and monitoring schedules, dates and resources.
records.evidence_quote: Networks are used as a basis for planning, analyzing, controlling and monitoring schedules, dates, and resources.

records.claim_text: SAP PS networks are activity-on-node graphs, not activity-on-arrow.
records.evidence_quote: In the Project System networks are activity-on-node networks.

records.claim_text: The network header carries assignments to project definition, WBS element or sales document plus default values.
records.evidence_quote: Assignments to other objects, for example, project definition, WBS element or sales document

records.claim_text: In header-assigned networks the header costing values are binding for the whole network rather than defaults.
records.evidence_quote: In header-assigned networks the values in the Costing section of the supplementary data screen of the network header are not default values

records.claim_text: Assigning a network header to a project definition allows the project dates to be copied into network basic dates.
records.evidence_quote: you can copy the dates from the project definition into the basic dates of the network.

records.claim_text: Assigning a network to a WBS element implies the project definition assignment automatically.
records.evidence_quote: the project definition will be copied automatically when the assignment is made.

records.claim_text: An activity has a duration, a defined start and finish, is uninterrupted, consumes resources and incurs costs.
records.evidence_quote: They have a defined start and a defined finish.

records.claim_text: Activities are resource-consuming: resources are required to execute them.
records.evidence_quote: Resources are needed to execute them.

records.claim_text: Internally processed activities capture work by machines or persons and feed capacity requirement planning.
records.evidence_quote: you determine the amount of Work produced by machines or persons, and use this information in resource planning to plan the capacity requirement.

records.claim_text: Externally processed activities represent services bought from other companies and run through purchasing.
records.evidence_quote: Using external processing you determine which services are required from other companies to carry out the project.

records.claim_text: Service activities plan planned and unplanned external services, procured through purchasing.
records.evidence_quote: Using External Services Management you plan unplanned and planned services for carrying out the project.

records.claim_text: General costs activities plan primary costs such as travel costs.
records.evidence_quote: you plan primary costs, for example, travel costs.

records.claim_text: Relationships determine the chronological sequence of activities within a network or standard network.
records.evidence_quote: Relationships determine the chronological sequence of activities in a network or a standard network.

records.claim_text: A relationship is directional: one activity is predecessor, the other successor.
records.evidence_quote: These dependencies are represented by relationships in which one activity is the predecessor or the successor of another activity.

records.claim_text: The relationship type governs how two activities are linked.
records.evidence_quote: The type of the relationship determines how the individual activities are linked with each other.

records.claim_text: Finish-Start links the end of one activity to the start of the following activity.
records.evidence_quote: This is the relationship between the end of an activity to the beginning of the following activity.

records.claim_text: Start-Finish relationships exist but are rarely used and are usually rewritten as Finish-Start.
records.evidence_quote: SF relationships are seldom used in practice

records.claim_text: A subnetwork covers part of a project and is linked by relationships to other subnetworks in the same project.
records.evidence_quote: A subnetwork is a network which covers only part of a project and is linked in relationships with other subnetworks in the same project.

records.claim_text: The superior network's network profile is not inherited by the subnetwork.
records.evidence_quote: The network profile for the superior network is not copied into the subnetwork.

records.claim_text: Network type and network parameters are defined in Customizing, not per project.
records.evidence_quote: In Customizing for the Project System you can define the network type and the network parameters.

records.claim_text: Milestones mark the transition between project phases or between departments.
records.evidence_quote: In general milestones are used to mark the transition between various phases or departments.

records.claim_text: Milestones can be created on networks, standard networks, WBS and standard WBS.
records.evidence_quote: You can create milestones in networks, standard networks, work breakdown structures (WBS) and standard work breakdown structures (standard WBS).

records.claim_text: Milestones cannot be attached to activity elements.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot create milestones for activity elements.

records.claim_text: When a milestone is reached its actual date is copied into the linked billing plan date.
records.evidence_quote: When the milestone is reached, the actual date of the milestone is copied into the billing plan.

records.claim_text: Milestone functions are predefined automations in networks that trigger a sequence of events.
records.evidence_quote: Predefined milestone functions are used in networks to trigger a sequence of events for a particular business process.

records.claim_text: A milestone function fires on either a system status change or a user status change when both are set.
records.evidence_quote: the system triggers the function both when the system status changes and when the user status changes.

records.claim_text: Activity milestones can create a network, release follow-up activities or start a workflow task.
records.evidence_quote: Milestones assigned to network activities enable the triggering of milestone functions, such as creating a new network, releasing follow-up activities, or starting a workflow task.

records.claim_text: MTA compares scheduled milestone dates captured on different report dates against plan.
records.evidence_quote: Milestone trend analysis is a simple method for analyzing the dates in a project and comparing them with planned data.

records.claim_text: In an MTA chart a horizontal curve means the project is running to plan.
records.evidence_quote: If the project runs according to plan, the curve remains horizontal.

records.claim_text: PS ships several standard (template) structures used to create operative structures.
records.evidence_quote: In the Project System there are several different standard structures that you can use as templates to create operative structures.

records.claim_text: Standardizing project structures makes projects more transparent and comparable for controlling.
records.evidence_quote: A further advantage of standardizing project structures is that it makes the processing of projects more transparent

records.claim_text: A standard WBS is a neutral, reusable template for creating operative work breakdown structures.
records.evidence_quote: Neutral work breakdown structure that can be used more than once and serves as a template for creating operative work breakdown structures.

records.claim_text: Standard networks can be linked to standard WBS so a template covers both structure and execution.
records.evidence_quote: You can link standard networks with standard work breakdown structures and so create templates

records.claim_text: Instantiating a standard network that is linked to a standard WBS also creates the operative WBS.
records.evidence_quote: When you use a standard network that is assigned to a standard WBS to create an operative network an operative WBS is also created.

records.claim_text: The reverse is not true: creating an operative WBS from a standard WBS does not create the network.
records.evidence_quote: However if you create an operative WBS from a standard WBS to which a standard network is assigned, an operative network is not created.

records.claim_text: A standard project definition is a neutral template used to create operative or further standard project definitions.
records.evidence_quote: Neutral project definition, which can be used to create operative project definitions or standard project definitions as templates.

records.claim_text: A standard network is a project-neutral network template for creating operative or further standard networks.
records.evidence_quote: Project-neutral network structure, which can be used as a template when creating other standard networks or operative networks.

records.claim_text: Standard WBS cannot hold operative data - no cost planning or time scheduling.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot use a standard WBS for cost planning or time scheduling purposes.

records.claim_text: Settlement rules cannot be maintained in standard WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: You also cannot maintain settlement rules in standard WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Only the standard WBS definition carries status; its elements have none.
records.evidence_quote: In the standard work breakdown structure, only the definition has a status.

records.claim_text: Standard WBS definitions carry three statuses: Created, Released and Closed.
records.evidence_quote: The status of the definition is Created (standard WBS) (CRES), Released (standard WBS) (RELS) or Closed (standard WBS) (CLOS).

records.claim_text: An operative WBS can be seeded from an existing WBS, a subtree of it, or a standard WBS.
records.evidence_quote: You can use an existing WBS, a section of the project hierarchy, or a standard WBS as a template.

records.claim_text: When copying WBS elements in, you choose whether the selected root itself is included or only its children.
records.evidence_quote: With root: The selected WBS element is included. Without root: Only the subordinate WBS elements are included.

records.claim_text: Copying a WBS element automatically brings its whole subordinate subtree with it.
records.evidence_quote: If the WBS element to be included has additional WBS elements subordinate to it, the system automatically copies these lower-level hierarchy elements.

records.claim_text: Copy, include, shift and delete always act on a WBS element together with its entire subtree.
records.evidence_quote: a WBS element is always copied, included, shifted, or deleted with all the WBS elements in its subtree.

records.claim_text: Indent moves the selected WBS element one level down into the preceding sibling's subtree.
records.evidence_quote: you shift the selected WBS element down one structure level to the subtree of the preceding WBS element.

records.claim_text: Outdent moves the element one level up, next to its former parent.
records.evidence_quote: you shift the selected WBS element up one structure level to the position next to its previous parent.

records.claim_text: Move up/down only reorders siblings; it never reparents a WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot move a WBS element to a new parent.

records.claim_text: Drag-and-drop semantics differ by drop target: between rows inserts as sibling, onto a row nests below it.
records.evidence_quote: Drop a WBS element on another WBS element to insert it at the structure level below this WBS element.

records.claim_text: New WBS element IDs are generated from the parent element ID and reused as the initial name.
records.evidence_quote: The system generates the WBS element ID based on the ID of the parent element and uses the same value for the WBS element name.

records.claim_text: A WBS element cannot be deleted once costs have been planned on it.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot delete WBS elements if you have already planned costs.

records.claim_text: System status controls which business transactions are permitted on a WBS or WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: The active system status determines which business transactions you can perform with work breakdown structures and WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Technically Completed marks work finished technically while further costs are still expected.
records.evidence_quote: WBS elements that are completed from a technical point of view, but where you still expect costs to accrue.

records.claim_text: Status propagates in both directions between a project/WBS element and its lower-level elements.
records.evidence_quote: The processing status of a project or WBS element influences the status of the lower-level WBS elements and vice versa.

records.claim_text: Releasing an element auto-releases all lower-level elements still in Created status.
records.evidence_quote: All the lower-level WBS elements that have the status Created are automatically released along with it.

records.claim_text: Partially Released is system-derived, never manually set, when any child is released.
records.evidence_quote: This status cannot be set manually. It is set automatically when any of the lower-level WBS elements are set to Released.

records.claim_text: A project version captures the state of a project at a point in time or at a status.
records.evidence_quote: A project version is created for operative structures or in the information system and captures the state of a project

records.claim_text: Plan versions are an accounting construct storing alternative cost plans for one project.
records.evidence_quote: A plan version is created in accounting and stores different cost plans for a project, such as an 'optimistic' and a 'pessimistic' plan.

records.claim_text: Selection versions are reporting-only snapshots of data matching selection criteria.
records.evidence_quote: A selection version is used only in the information system for processing in the background

records.claim_text: When creating a version you choose full current data or only the selected subset.
records.evidence_quote: When you create project versions in the information system, you can choose whether you want all of the current data or a subset of data.

records.claim_text: An MTA-relevant flag on a version marks it usable for milestone trend analysis.
records.evidence_quote: The MTA-relevant indicator in this window stipulates that the data from this version can be used in milestone trend analysis.

records.claim_text: Project versions are written asynchronously, not in real time.
records.evidence_quote: Project versions are not created in real time.

records.claim_text: Multiple project versions are compared side by side in the structure overview, colour-coded per version.
records.evidence_quote: The different project versions are displayed in different colors.

records.claim_text: A version profile decides whether status-dependent versions are written and with which data.
records.evidence_quote: The Version Profile determines whether status-dependent project versions are written and with which data.

records.claim_text: Simulation lets a project be changed and saved without touching the operative project.
records.evidence_quote: it is often necessary to simulate and save changes to a project, without affecting the operative project.

records.claim_text: Simulation versions carry no system statuses.
records.evidence_quote: There are no system statuses in simulation versions.

records.claim_text: A simulation profile controls which texts move to and from simulation versions.
records.evidence_quote: The Simulation Profile determines which texts are copied to and from simulation versions.

records.claim_text: Project Builder is the single-transaction editor for the whole project structure.
records.evidence_quote: You can create, change or display all project structure data in one transaction.

records.claim_text: All WBS and network editing transactions are reachable from within Project Builder.
records.evidence_quote: All the editing transactions for work breakdown structures and networks can be executed in the Project Builder.

records.claim_text: Project Builder offers a user-specific worklist and a user-specific templates pool.
records.evidence_quote: You can define a user-specific worklist and a user-specific templates pool.

records.claim_text: The project hierarchy is shown in a dedicated persistent screen area beside the detail work area.
records.evidence_quote: The hierarchy of your current project is displayed in a separate screen area.

records.claim_text: The structure pane shows current project data together with its hierarchical relationships.
records.evidence_quote: The structure contains the selected project data of the current project, along with its hierarchical relationships.

records.claim_text: Project Builder maintains every PS object except Production Resources/Tools assignment.
records.evidence_quote: You can use the Project Builder to maintain any object in the SAP PS, except for the assignment of Production Resources/Tools (PRT).

records.claim_text: WBS element detail is organised into named tabs including basic data, assignments, responsibilities and control data.
records.evidence_quote: The following table provides you with an overview of where you can edit detailed data for individual WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Assigning an investment profile and releasing the WBS element generates the asset under construction.
records.evidence_quote: By assigning an investment profile to the project or WBS element and upon releasing the WBS element, the asset under construction is generated.

records.claim_text: PS splits structures into operative structures (WBS, networks) and standard structures used for reuse.
records.evidence_quote: A clearly and unambiguously structured project is the basis for its planning, monitoring, control and success.

records.claim_text: Networks represent individual project activities together with their relationships.
records.evidence_quote: Networks are used to represent the individual project activities, together with their relationships.

records.claim_text: Hierarchies enable both top-down budget/responsibility assignment and bottom-up aggregation of costs, revenue, dates and progress.
records.evidence_quote: Bottom-up estimates (for example, to evaluate aggregated data about costs, revenues, scheduling, and progress).

gaps: No Tier-1 SAP page was found that enumerates the three operative indicators (planning element / account assignment element / billing element) together in one sentence; the tri-part definition rests on learning.sap.com (Tier 2). Tier-1 corroboration exists for billing element and for account-assignment-element-as-network-prerequisite only.

Standard Milestone / Milestone Group definition page (legacy GUID c5/72bb53707db44ce10000000a174cb4) returns an empty body on the saphelp_me150 tree; standard milestones are only evidenced indirectly via the Creating Milestones page's link text.
No evidenced statement of a hard maximum number of WBS hierarchy levels was found. Only the 24-character WBS ID cap and the mask-separator requirement constrain depth. Do NOT assume a level ceiling.

The classic SAP PS library (saphelp_pserv472) is behind an S-user login; all PS structure prose had to be sourced from the saphelp_me150 static mirror and from help.sap.com/docs via the in-app browser.

help.sap.com/docs pages are a JS SPA: WebFetch returns only the title. Every /docs citation in this file was rendered with the in-app browser. Downstream lanes should reuse the GUID-to-legacy-static-route mapping documented in search_log rather than WebFetch on /docs.
Lead/lag time intervals on relationships, float/slack calculation, scheduling algorithms, and the project planning board Gantt were not researched in depth - out of R01 structural scope but adjacent.

Two source families were mixed: classic on-premise SAP PS (project definition + WBS + networks) and S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects (projects + WBS elements, no networks). Billing-element nesting, indent/outdent and processing-status cascade records come from the Cloud variant and may not hold verbatim in classic PS.
No SAP Fiori design-guideline citation was attempted in this lane; UX-PATTERN records here are behavioural descriptions taken from product documentation, not from the Fiori design system.
